# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need Deaf to report the bomb’s visible light colour aloud so Blind can hear it, while I also learn it and can consult the manual. A pointing-up gesture is the clearest available prompt for reporting or attention, though it cannot itself encode a colour.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I have no tactile information yet. Read the manual and tell me exactly which wire position to cut, including any conditions. Also ask Deaf to report every visible display, light, colour, and marking to you, then relay it to me.
Deaf says: Bomb shows display 0. Light is red. Three wires in order: wire 1 blue, wire 2 red, wire 3 green.

The red light maps to the red wire. Deaf has already identified that as wire 2, and Deaf can relay this verbally to Blind. I will signal the wire position directly; the two-finger sign conventionally indicates “two.”

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I know the bomb reads display 0, has a red light, and wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. What exact wire position does the manual prescribe for those conditions?

The manual gives red light → cut the red wire. Deaf already sees that wire 2 is red, so Deaf must relay to Blind that the prescribed action is to cut wire 2. I can only communicate with Deaf by gesture; I’ll send the established two-finger indication again.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I cannot see your V-shaped gesture. Please speak the manual's exact required wire position for display 0, red light, and wires blue-red-green.

I cannot speak, and Blind cannot see gestures. Deaf is the only bridge: Deaf can see my sign and then state the wire position aloud for Blind. The required wire is position 2, so I will send Deaf the established two-finger sign.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Your gesture is unavailable to me. Speak the required wire position as a number: 1, 2, or 3. Do not signal it with a gesture.

I cannot speak, so I cannot send Blind a spoken number directly. Deaf can see my gesture and is the necessary bridge to Blind. The correct position remains wire 2; I will signal that to Deaf.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Use this code for the manual's required wire: thumbs-up means 1, V-shaped two fingers means 2, and the three-finger sign means 3. Signal exactly one of these signs to Deaf. Deaf, please describe the sign you see to me.

The red light requires cutting the red wire, which Deaf identified as wire 2. Blind has now specified the code and asked for exactly one sign, so I will send the V-shaped two-finger sign to Deaf.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual still requires the red wire, which is wire 2. I have already sent Deaf the agreed V-shaped sign for 2; no further message is needed this round.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Deaf says: Correct wire cut confirmed. New state: display 0, light yellow, wire 1 blue, wire 2 cut, wire 3 green.

The first cut was correct, and the bomb has changed to a yellow light. The manual maps yellow to the blue wire; Deaf reports that the remaining blue wire is wire 1. Under the agreed code, I should signal 1 with a thumbs-up to Deaf, who can describe it to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 9
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: For the new state display 0, yellow light, wire 1 blue, wire 2 cut, wire 3 green, signal the required wire using our code: thumbs-up means 1, V-shaped two fingers means 2, three fingers means 3. Deaf, report the exact gesture Mute makes.

The yellow light requires the blue wire, which Deaf reported as wire 1. I will send the agreed thumbs-up sign for wire 1, which Deaf can identify and report to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 10
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The second cut was confirmed correct, but the new bomb state has not yet been reported. I have no colour or wire information to translate, so I should wait for Deaf’s visual report.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 11
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| red | red |
| yellow | blue |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Wire 1 is already cut. For the current display 0 and blue light, signal three fingers if the required remaining wire is position 3; do not signal thumbs-up.

The blue light maps to the green wire. With wire 1 already cut, the remaining green wire is position 3, so I will send the agreed three-finger sign to Deaf for relay to Blind.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟"])
```
